BiblicalUsage: That which is sown — the seed in the ground, the thing planted — is the word's plain sense. Leviticus asks whether sowing seed falls on a clean carcass, and Isaiah promises that as the earth brings forth her bud, so the LORD will cause righteousness to spring forth. Sowing is the picture; springing up is the promise.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God delights to grow what is sown: righteousness springs up the way a field does, because He causes it.
